title: Array Memory And Measurement Lab
briefing: Predict array memory and runtime before measuring them, then preserve enough evidence for another learner to reproduce the result.
objectives: Calculate tensor payload from shape and dtype before allocation.
Compare a reference loop with vectorized NumPy while preserving correctness.
Separate a measured observation from an explanation that still needs evidence.

prediction.prompt: What happens to the payload size when a fixed-shape array changes from float32 to float64?

steps.title: Write the budget
steps.instructions: Choose two shapes and calculate element count and payload bytes for float32 and float64 before running any code.

steps.title: Verify payload
steps.instructions: Create the arrays with NumPy, compare nbytes with each prediction, and explain any mismatch without changing the original prediction.

steps.title: Benchmark correctly
steps.instructions: Test a loop and a vectorized equivalent for correctness, warm both paths, run repeated timings, and report the median with environment details.

evidenceChecklist.label: Python, NumPy, input, and machine details are recorded

reflectionPrompts: Which result was observation, and which part of your explanation remains a hypothesis?
What temporary allocations might the concise NumPy expression hide?
extensionChallenge: Change the input size until memory pressure or cache behavior changes the timing trend, then state the boundary you observed.
